domain_entities.name: AccrualPeriod
domain_entities.purpose: Value object describing the half-open accrual window [start, end) produced by periodContaining; the single canonical shape consumed by both the leave and balance paths.

business_rules: startOfUtcDay must derive the UTC-midnight instant from the input's UTC calendar fields (getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate) and never from local-time fields; the result is Date.UTC(y, m, d). This is load-bearing: node-pg parses date columns to local midnight while this arithmetic reads UTC fields, and any drift silently shifts every accrual period by a day on a non-UTC server. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever startOfUtcDay appears, not only here]

addMonths advances the calendar month by the given offset and clamps the day-of-month to the last day of the target month (e.g. Jan 31 + 1 → Feb 28/29; Mar 31 + 1 → Apr 30). It must not mutate its input. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever addMonths appears, not only here]

periodContaining returns a half-open accrual period [start, end): a date belongs to the period when start <= date < end (start inclusive, end exclusive). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever periodContaining appears, not only here]

periodContaining rejects any date strictly before the accrual anchor with ConflictError('Requested date precedes the accrual anchor'). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever periodContaining appears, not only here]

periodContaining steps at most 10,000 periods from the anchor and throws ConflictError('Unable to resolve accrual period') if no period resolves within that bound. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever periodContaining appears, not only here]

Each of startOfUtcDay, addMonths, and periodContaining has exactly one definition in the repository, located in src/shared/date/accrual.ts; all consumers (leave and balance services) import them from the shared entry point rather than maintaining private copies. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever startOfUtcDay / addMonths / periodContaining appears, not only here]

The three accrual date helpers are pure UTC functions: their results depend only on the input Date's UTC fields and are independent of the host timezone (TZ environment). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever startOfUtcDay / addMonths / periodContaining appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
This feature is a pure refactor (deduplication) with no new entities, no new lifecycle states, and no behavioral change. The domain slice is therefore minimal.

Domain concept: AccrualPeriod — a value object { start, end } describing the half-open accrual window [start, end) produced by periodContaining. It is the single canonical shape consumed by both the leave and balance paths. It has no lifecycle states (it is an immutable value, not a stateful entity).

The three canonical UTC accrual date helpers — startOfUtcDay, addMonths, periodContaining — are the domain's foundational date-arithmetic semantics. Their behavior is BINDING and must hold identically at every call site (scope "broad"), which is exactly why this feature collapses the duplicated private copies into the single shared definition in src/shared/date/accrual.ts:

- startOfUtcDay: derives UTC midnight from the input's UTC calendar fields (getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate), never local-time fields. Load-bearing: node-pg parses date columns to local midnight while this arithmetic reads UTC fields; any drift shifts every accrual period by a day on a non-UTC server.
- addMonths: advances the calendar month and clamps day-of-month to the last day of the target month; must not mutate its input.
- periodContaining: returns a half-open period [start, end) (start inclusive, end exclusive); rejects date < anchor with ConflictError('Requested date precedes the accrual anchor'); steps at most 10,000 periods and throws ConflictError('Unable to resolve accrual period') on exhaustion.
- All three are pure UTC functions independent of the host timezone (TZ).

No lifecycle states are introduced or changed by this feature, so there is nothing new to fold into architectureMdUpdate beyond the existing canonical states already documented (LeaveRequest DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED; LeaveBalance OPEN/CLOSED; etc.). The deduplication invariant — exactly one definition of each helper, imported from the shared entry point by both leave and balance services — is recorded as a broad business rule so a future re-introduction of a private copy is caught.

No open questions: the feature is a pure move with behavior explicitly frozen (no arithmetic "improvements" permitted).
